clinician.final_diagnosis: ATM in the context of recent COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old man presented with progressive bilateral lower limb weakness, urinary retention, constipation, and patchy paresthesia following a recent COVID-19 infection. Neurological exam showed signs consistent with an upper motor neuron lesion. Spinal MRI revealed a long segment of T2 signal elevation in the spinal cord from T7 to T10, without enhancement or mass (E007). Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated protein but normal glucose, with negative cultures and negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR (E009). Serum testing for autoimmune antibodies (anti-myelin-associated glycoprotein IgM, MOG-IgG, NMO-IgG) was negative (E011). The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisone for 3 days and intensive physiotherapy (E015). Following treatment, neurological symptoms improved significantly, and a repeat MRI on day 10 showed almost complete resolution of the spinal cord changes (E016, E017). He regained full lower limb motor strength, paresthesias resolved, and the indwelling catheter was removed, leading to discharge on day 11 (E017).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with progressive bilateral lower limb weakness, urinary retention, constipation, lower limb stiffness, difficulty walking, and patchy paresthesia to the level of the umbilicus, following a recent COVID-19 infection.
Neurological exam showed increased tone, hyperreflexia, reduced proprioception of lower limbs, patchy paresthesia to umbilicus, and decreased anal tone, consistent with an upper motor neuron lesion.
Spinal MRI demonstrated a long segment of T2 signal elevation centrally in the spinal cord from T7 to T10, without significant enhancement or mass.
CSF analysis showed elevated protein (0.79 g/L) but normal glucose, with negative CSF and blood cultures, and no SARS-CoV-2 detected by PCR in CSF or nasopharyngeal swab.
Serum antibodies for anti-myelin-associated glycoprotein IgM, myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG-IgG), and neuromyelitis optica IgG (NMO-IgG) were negative.
The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisone 1 g per day for 3 days and intensive physiotherapy.
Neurological symptoms improved shortly after corticosteroid therapy, with regained full lower limb motor strength, resolved paresthesias, and successful removal of the indwelling catheter.
Follow-up MRI on day 10 showed almost complete resolution of the T2 changes in the spinal cord between T7 and T10.
